topSignals.title: FERC RM26-4 abeyance filings due today — LCOE model trigger pending in 24 hours
topSignals.text: — August 3 is the 45-day deadline for all six RTOs/ISOs (PJM, MISO, CAISO, ISO-NE, NYISO, SPP) to submit abeyance requests under FERC's June 18 show cause orders. ISO-NE confirmed August 1 it would file for 90-day abeyance; other RTOs expected to follow. FERC has stated it will "heavily scrutinize" requests and limit any abeyance to 90 days (running to November 16). If any abeyance is denied: August 17 hard tariff-reform deadline immediately activates. LCOE model action: update August 4 after FERC publishes its response — activate $5–20/MWh avoided-T-cost input if denied; hold as November 16 placeholder if granted. FERC RM26-4 docket | McGuireWoods analysis

topSignals.title: Elcogen E3000 G2 technical paper now public on ResearchGate (EFCF 2026) — first quantitative performance data
topSignals.text: — The conference paper "Introduction to Elcogen elcoStack E3000 Generation 2 Solid Oxide Technology" is now accessible on ResearchGate, emerging from the EFCF 2026 proceedings (Lucerne, June 30–July 3). Key disclosed figures: >75% electrical efficiency in fuel cell mode, 90% total efficiency with waste heat recovery, 33 kWh/kg H2 in SOEC mode, zero degradation under thermal cycling capability tests, and performance improvement observed over 23,000 rapid current cycles in electrolysis mode. This is the first quantitative post-launch performance disclosure for the E3000 G2 (platform launched May 2026 at World Hydrogen Summit, Rotterdam). Thermal cycling stability and current-cycle durability directly validate the data-center dynamic-load use case. LCOE flag: stack replacement interval better than conservative degradation assumptions — update when full peer-reviewed paper is accessible and stack-vs-system efficiency boundary is confirmed. ResearchGate paper | Elcogen E3000 G2 product page

topSignals.title: Meta + Oklo 1.2 GW nuclear campus, Pike County OH — confirmed 2030+ timeline (new to digest)
topSignals.text: — Announced January 9, 2026 but first appearance in this digest: Meta Platforms prepays for power and funds Oklo's Aurora microreactor development to build a scalable 1.2 GW nuclear energy campus in Pike County, Ohio serving Meta's regional data centers and AI supercluster. First power realistically 2030+ given NRC licensing timelines for Oklo's Aurora design. Adds to the growing list of hyperscaler nuclear hedges (Crusoe/Aalo 50 MWe INL 2027; Microsoft TMI restart 2027; Amazon Talen PPA). Pattern confirmed: hyperscalers treat nuclear as the 2030+ baseload option and SOFCs as the 2025–2029 deployment bridge — not a substitution. Oklo PR

items.text: Elcogen: E3000 G2 technical paper on ResearchGate — see Top Signal #2. Key specs: >75% FC electrical efficiency (stack level); 90% total with heat recovery; 33 kWh/kg H2 (SOEC); zero thermal cycling degradation; performance improvement across 23,000 rapid current cycles. ELCO I Tallinn factory (360 MW/yr) continuing production and G2 deliveries. Next watch: full EFCF 2026 proceedings release and potential peer-reviewed publication. Caution: confirm whether efficiency figures are stack-only LHV or net system electrical before applying to LCOE model.

Topsoe: Quiet day. Status unchanged from August 2. Herning SOEC factory hibernated pending commercial-scale H2 demand; CEO Elena Scaltritti (since June 1, 2026). SOFC/data-center pathway deferred to 2029+. FY2026 guidance: DKK 7,600–8,400M revenue, EBIT margin 4–9% (revised from 0–5%).
Other players: Quiet day. No new announcements from Bloom Energy (technology), Ceres Power, SolydEra, Mitsubishi Power, Kyocera, Aisin, or FuelCell Energy for August 3.

Quiet day for new deployment announcements. Active pipeline unchanged: Oracle Project Jupiter (2.45 GW NM, air permit public hearing October 19, NM AG investigation ongoing), Crusoe Cheyenne (900 MW Phase 1 Bloom SOFCs, Aalo nuclear demo INL 2027 as long-term hedge), FCEL/Fit Energy (380 MW total, 30 MW initial delivery H2 2026), Equinix >100 MW across 19+ DCs, Bloom/Brookfield $5B deployment fund, Nebius 328 MW EaaS.

FERC RM26-4 — abeyance filings due today (see Top Signal #1). No FERC response yet; outcome expected August 4–5. If abeyance denied: August 17 tariff-reform deadline is live. If granted: November 16 stakeholder filing deadline. LCOE model update deferred to August 4.

Quiet otherwise. NY moratorium (50 MW+ threshold, islanded exemption active), EU CADA (rating scheme still under development), Germany EnEfG (PUE ≤1.2, ERF ≥10%, 15% waste heat reuse from July 2026): no changes from August 2.

Meta + Oklo 1.2 GW nuclear campus, Pike County OH (Jan 2026, new to digest) — See Top Signal #3. Pattern: hyperscalers hedge SOFCs with nuclear MOUs while nuclear first-power timelines remain 2030+. SOFC 90-day deployment advantage unchallenged through 2029.

Crusoe + Aalo Atomics (covered August 2): 50 MWe Aalo Pod at INL (2027 demo), portfolio-wide target end-2029 — most advanced commercial nuclear-AI timeline. Still confirms 2029 as the earliest realistic nuclear displacement date for SOFCs.

Bulletin of the Atomic Scientists (July 2026) "Don't fall for Big Tech's PR hype" on nuclear: HALEU fuel supply chains absent, licensing multi-year, timelines 10+ years — reinforces structural SOFC opportunity through at least 2029.
No new gas turbine, SMR, PEM hydrogen, or battery-storage competitive announcements identified for August 3.

Bloom Energy (BE): August 2 intraday range $198.59–$235.49; close approximately $201–210 (sources vary). Recovery from $159.80 July 31 intraday trough is confirmed. 29-analyst consensus PT $273.51 (+29% implied upside). All analyst PTs remain above current price. Q3 2026 earnings (October) next catalyst. FY2026 guidance (raised July 28): $3.9–4.2B revenue, $2.55–2.85 non-GAAP EPS, $800–900M operating income. StockAnalysis.com | Yahoo Finance
FuelCell Energy (FCEL): ~$21.60 (August 2 range $21.50–$25.70). Quiet day. $225M equity offering (July 7–8) overhang persists. Q3 FY2026 earnings (October) next catalyst. CNBC

Ceres Power (LON: CWR): Quiet. ~−40% from June peak. H1 2026 results (September) next catalyst; first royalties received from licensees (commercial-scale manufacturing now active) confirm structural health.

Elcogen E3000 G2 — EFCF 2026 paper (ResearchGate): See Top Signal #2 and Stack & Cell Technology. The >75% FC electrical efficiency figure, if reproducible at ELCO I (360 MW/yr) production scale, would set a new commercial stack benchmark. For context: Bloom Energy's published system-level efficiency is ~60–65% LHV; Elcogen's >75% appears to be stack-level (before BOP parasitic losses). Confirm boundary definition before updating LCOE model. At system level, 90% total efficiency with heat recovery aligns with the RSER hybrid integration review (S1364032125013097) benchmark. ResearchGate

Quiet day for new peer-reviewed system-level SOFC papers. Prior active references unchanged: RSER hybrid integration review (S1364032125013097), SOFC-GT-sCO2 TEA (S036031992501359X), EPFL Nat. Commun. 17:2421 (66.3% efficiency modular design).
No new system-level SOFC TEA/LCOE papers identified for August 3.

Carry-forward watch: "Recent developments in control and integration of solid oxide fuel cells: From stack to system" (RSER, ScienceDirect S1364032125006732) — covers SOFC BOP, anode off-gas recirculation (AOGR), multi-stack, and energy buffer integration with dynamic control. System-level scope directly relevant to data-center load-following simulation. Confirm publication date; may be late-2025 work not yet cited in digest.

lcoe.text: Elcogen E3000 G2 stack efficiency >75% FC / 90% total (EFCF 2026 paper): If confirmed at system boundary, implies ~20% higher net electrical output per unit fuel vs. Bloom Energy's ~60–65% published system efficiency. Before updating LCOE model: (a) verify whether figure is stack-only LHV or net system electrical at system boundary; (b) confirm at ELCO I production scale, not just test-bench cells. Action: obtain full paper; flag for LCOE model update once verified.

FERC RM26-4 avoided-T-cost (today's deadline): Hold $5–20/MWh as LCOE placeholder. Update August 4. If abeyance denied: activate as live input for PJM/MISO/CAISO/ISO-NE on-site SOFC vs. grid comparison. If granted: defer to November 16 stakeholder filing date.

BE stock $201–210 (August 2): WACC sensitivity band: maintain 10–10.5%. If BE holds above $220 through week end, revise toward 9.5–10%. Bloom's EaaS $/MWh pricing reflects its cost of capital — lower WACC = lower bundled power rate to customers.

Meta/Oklo nuclear timeline — competitive modeling: Do not introduce nuclear as a competing LCOE scenario before 2030. Maintain SOFC as the sole commercially available 24/7 baseload on-site option for AI data centers through 2028–2029.

Pending (carry-forward): Bloom 10-Q (due by September 11 = 45 days from July 28 earnings) for explicit shipped MW in Q2 and actual revenue-per-kW. Elcogen E3000 G2 system-level efficiency confirmation. FERC RM26-4 outcome August 4.
